decision: Add Config CTE to pipeline-views/02_etb_ss_calc.sql to eliminate magic numbers (100, 60, 45, 20000, 1)
rationale: ETB_SS_CALC had five magic numbers scattered through SSCalculation and the final WHERE clause. Centralising them in a Config CTE ensures a single authoritative source for every threshold, making future business-rule changes a one-line edit rather than a grep-and-replace across the formula.
alternatives_considered: Leave magic numbers as comments only (insufficient — code still brittle)
Use SQL variables instead of CTE (incompatible with view syntax in SQL Server)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (SELECT 100 AS Lead_Days_Series_30, 60 AS Lead_Days_Series_10, 45 AS Lead_Days_Default, 20000 AS SS_Value_Ceiling, 1 AS Demand_Lookback_Years)

decision: Add Config CTE to sql/03_etb_wfq_pipe.sql and CROSS JOIN Config to WHERE clauses
rationale: The sql/ version of View 3 had the same magic numbers (21, 14, 65, 90) as inline literals, while the pipeline-views/ version already had a Config CTE. Aligning both versions eliminates drift and ensures the sql/ production script matches the hardened reference implementation.
alternatives_considered: Regenerate sql/ from pipeline-views/ (would overwrite other sql/-specific changes)
Only fix pipeline-views/ version (leaves sql/ production at risk)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (...) ... CROSS JOIN Config WHERE ... <= (SELECT Lot_Age_Limit_Days FROM Config)

decision: Add documentation header + Config CTE + UNASSIGNED vendor guard to sql/06_etb_run_risk.sql
rationale: View 6 was the only production view missing all three quality markers (header, Config CTE, UNASSIGNED fallback). The COALESCE(d.PRIME_VNDR, ss.PRIME_VNDR) without a final fallback could silently produce NULL vendors if both sources were missing — a violation of Issue 4. Adding 'UNASSIGNED' as the third COALESCE argument closes the gap with zero logic change.
alternatives_considered: Add only Config CTE without UNASSIGNED guard (partial fix — NULL vendor risk remains)
Refactor vendor resolution to match View 7 four-tier hierarchy (scope creep for this pass)

decision: Add Config CTE to sql/07_etb_buyer_control.sql covering all five magic number categories
rationale: View 7 had the most dispersed magic numbers (0.25, 50.00, 30, 1.5, 12) spread across three CTEs. Grouping them in a single Config CTE with business-rule comments creates a self-documenting configuration layer that buyers and analysts can inspect without reading the formula CTEs.
alternatives_considered: Split into domain-specific Config CTEs per logical group (over-engineering for single-view scope)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (SELECT 30 AS Default_Lead_Days, 0.25 AS Default_Holding_Cost_Pct, 50.00 AS Order_Cost_Per_PO, 1.5 AS EOQ_Fallback_Deficit_Multiplier, 12 AS Annual_Demand_Months_Factor)

decision: Use string constants in Config CTE for Pattern A suppression labels in sql/08_etb_v_client_295_stockouts.sql
rationale: The suppression status strings ('BEGINNING BALANCE', 'SUPPRESSED: Stale & Unissued', 'SUPPRESSED: Full Coverage in Fence') are repeated verbatim in two separate WHERE clauses within the same view. A typo in one clause would silently break Pattern A noise exclusion without error. Centralising the strings in Config makes both WHERE clauses reference the same authoritative values.
alternatives_considered: Use a NOT IN list referencing a helper CTE (equivalent — chose Config for consistency with other views)
sql_pattern: Config AS (SELECT 'BEGINNING BALANCE' AS Status_Beg_Bal, 'SUPPRESSED: Stale & Unissued' AS Status_Stale, ...)
